content.readme: # Lichii Lichii is an experimental, open-source Nintendo Switch and Switch 2 emulator written in C++. It builds on Eglantine, Eden, yuzu and Sudachi, preserving their contributions while developing this fork's game compatibility and renderer fixes. This is an independent fork, not an official release of those upstream projects. Lichii is not affiliated with Nintendo. Visit the [official Lichii website](https://lichii.zortos.me) to find games and compare community compatibility reports. ## Downloads and setup Download Lichii only from this repository's [releases page](https://github.com/zortos293/Lichii/releases). Lichii has no other download site: archives offered elsewhere, such as lichii.org, are not built by this project, and one has been reported to install malware ([#545](https://github.com/zortos293/Lichii/issues/545)). On Windows, extract the entire build archive and run **lichii.exe**. Only use games and system files you have legally obtained. Games, keys and firmware are not included. ### Existing saves and settings The rebrand intentionally retains the existing Eden/Eglantine data directories and configuration keys. It does not move or delete saves, settings or shader caches. Back up your saves before testing experimental builds. ## Compatibility and issue reports Compatibility and performance vary by game, hardware and driver. Rendering errors, stutters and crashes remain possible. Passing automated tests does not establish that a game renders correctly, and this project makes no universal frame-rate guarantee. Browse [community compatibility reports](https://lichii.zortos.me/reports) for results with each player's build and setup. Desktop reporting requires a build containing [PR #303](https://github.com/zortos293/Lichii/pull/303) and is not available in build 88. In builds that include it, play and stop a Switch 2 game, then right-click that game and choose **Submit compatibility report**. Only the latest session in the current Lichii process is eligible. Confirm the matching website catalog entry and review the editable machine, game, setup, and enabled add-on details prefilled where available. Check the public preview and give explicit consent before submitting. Nothing uploads automatically, and the native v1 reporter does not read or upload logs or files. When [reporting an issue](https://github.com/zortos293/Eglantine/issues), include: - The exact build, game version, CPU, GPU and driver version. - Relevant settings and steps to reproduce the problem. - A screenshot and the log from the affected session, after checking it for personal information. Do not upload game files, keys, firmware or private account information. ## Building and contributing See the [build guide](docs/Build.md), [user documentation](docs/user/README.md) and [coding guidelines](docs/Coding.md). Some inherited documentation and internal build target names still use upstream names. The GUI build target remains `yuzu`; its output is `lichii.exe` on Windows and `lichii` on other desktop platforms. Keep changes focused and distinguish code-level checks from actual gameplay testing. ## Artwork Art created by YOB (yobslab) The supplied Lichii logo, icon and library artwork are in [dist/branding](dist/branding). Windows, Linux and macOS icon resources are generated from that artwork by [Generate-LichiiIcons.ps1](tools/Generate-LichiiIcons.ps1). ## Support Lichii Lichii is free and stays free. If you want to help, you can donate in crypto. Donations help pay for the AI tools and build machines used to develop this open-source project faster. **Solana (SOL)** ```text JepEjfyWjGjhJvHSrqj52KtLjcbbbmUh1iGqerYBF4w ``` **Ethereum (ETH)** ```text 0x055ABa1b80Bc35C836Ce7E9F47c2b3d6C75b5534 ``` **Bitcoin (BTC)** ```text bc1qcvxdpf4qvdhqp8ee4s355cjmxrzsphsdwpl8w4 ``` **BNB Smart Chain (BNB)** ```text 0x055ABa1b80Bc35C836Ce7E9F47c2b3d6C75b5534 ``` **Polygon** ```text 0x055ABa1b80Bc35C836Ce7E9F47c2b3d6C75b5534 ``` Send each coin on its matching network. Coins sent on the wrong network can't be recovered. > [!NOTE] > Donations are voluntary gifts and are non-refundable. A donation does not buy any product, service, perk, early access, exclusive build, priority support or say in the project. Every release stays free and public for everyone. ## Credits and license Lichii inherits the work of the Eglantine, Eden, yuzu and Sudachi projects and their contributors, including Eglantine's original developer Camille LaVey. Original copyright notices and third-party licenses are retained. See [LICENSE.txt](LICENSE.txt) and the source files for applicable license terms.

# Uncharted: The Nathan Drake Collection for Windows

**Uncharted 1, 2 and 3 from the PS4 collection running natively on Windows 10 and 11, by [SuperMedo](https://github.com/Supermedo).** Mohammed Albarghouthi

Same idea as my [Bloodborne port](https://github.com/Supermedo/bloodborne_pc): the original PS4 game
code runs directly on your PC and the graphics are translated to Vulkan. Unpack the zip, start
`Uncharted.exe`, pick your game folder, choose a game and press **PLAY**.

**[Download the latest version](https://github.com/Supermedo/uncharted_pc/releases/latest)** · **[Join the Discord](https://discord.gg/s3RgH6cRfJ)**

> **No game files are included.** You need your own decrypted dump of the collection
> (CUSA02343, CUSA02320, ...: the folder with eboot.bin, big2-ps4_Shipping.elf,
> big3-ps4_Shipping.elf, sce_sys, u1data, u2data and u3data).
> This project is not affiliated with Sony Interactive Entertainment or Naughty Dog.

## Features

- All three games from one launcher: Drake's Fortune, Among Thieves and Drake's Deception.
- 60 FPS like on PS4, or 120 FPS (higher rates are experimental).
- Render resolution above 1080p (up to 3200x1800) and ultrawide aspect ratios: the games draw a real larger or wider picture, set in the launcher.
- Anti-aliasing with TAA, AMD FSR 3.1, AMD FSR 4 or NVIDIA DLSS (DLAA).
- Frame generation: AMD FSR 3 (any GPU) or NVIDIA DLSS (RTX 40 2x, RTX 50 up to 4x).
- Keyboard, mouse and controller together, all remappable. Mouse look in U3.
- Stereo, 5.1 or 7.1 sound: the games are told the real speaker layout (it follows the Windows setting, or pick it in the launcher).
- Trophies: the games' own trophy lists in the launcher, and a notice in the game when you earn one.
- Button prompts for keyboard and mouse, Xbox or PlayStation controllers; controller vibration settings.
- Cheats page (infinite health and ammo per game), launcher languages, your own covers and Steam art.
- A Fixes page for fixes that cost speed: Automatic turns each one on only where it helps.
- Add to Steam and desktop shortcuts from the launcher, automatic updates.

## Requirements

- Windows 10 (1903 or later) or Windows 11, 64-bit.
- An Intel Core 3rd generation (Ivy Bridge) or newer, an AMD Ryzen, or an AMD FX. Older Intel CPUs
  with AVX (Core 2nd and 3rd generation, Xeon E3 v1/v2): experimental, see Known problems.
- A graphics card with Vulkan 1.3 and a current driver, with **6 GB of video memory or more**.
  4 GB cards (GTX 1650, RX 570) run out of video memory and crash after a while; on those, keep
  Anti-aliasing and Frame generation off.
- About 8 GB of free memory (RAM + page file).

## Known problems

- **Uncharted 3, Cartagena square (chapter 2):** at high frame rates (240 Hz setting, ~80 FPS)
  the game could freeze and close with "GPU crash: the graphics device was lost". It came from
  the speed fix for that area and is fixed in 0.3. If it still happens to you, set Frame rate to
  60 on the Display page and open an issue with your `user\last_run.log`.
- **Uncharted 3:** green or black shapes flashing on Sully's shirt in Cartagena: the cloth
  solvers raced on NVIDIA's 32-lane groups. Fixed in 0.3.9 with BilalReloaded's fix.
- **Crash with "ASSERTION: GetRenderFrameParams(frameToFreeInstancesFor)->m_gfxEopTick"**
  (mostly U1 after the first cutscene): the game expected the GPU side to be done with a frame it
  wanted to reuse, and stopped when it wasn't yet (shaders building on a first run). Fixed in
  0.3.2 (0.3.4 for the 1.02 versions): the game now waits for it. If you still see it, open an
  issue with your log.
- **Intel HD / UHD graphics:** a black screen on the HD 630 is fixed in 0.3.3. Older Intel chips
  (HD 520) can still crash inside Intel's own driver.
- **Uncharted 3 London bar crash** (fault at `0xd9c59b`, or device lost in the bar fight): fixed in
  0.3.4.
- **Uncharted 2 loading crashes** (`ReadSync file (req/read: ...)`, white textures then
  `iSubMesh < m_numSubMeshInstances`): file reads could come back cut short. Fixed in 0.3.5.
- **Older CPUs:** the games use instructions of the PS4's processor (AVX, BMI1, MOVBE, LZCNT).
  Since 0.3.7 they are rewritten on CPUs that lack them, so Intel Core 3rd generation (Ivy Bridge)
  runs, as does AMD FX. Sandy Bridge (2nd generation) also lacks F16C and is not supported.
- **Random crashes with "execute access to 0" or a fault at `0x63f5d0` (U1):** Windows wrote its
  exception data over values the game keeps just below the stack pointer. Fixed in 0.3.7.
- **Uncharted 2, train wreck:** `IsFinite(deltaTransform)` in character-leg-ik.cpp, fixed in 0.3.6
  for the EU 1.00 version.
- Frame rates above 120 are experimental.

## Building

MSYS2 CLANG64 on Windows: `bash build.sh` builds `out\bb-probe.exe`, and
`bash packaging/windows/package.sh` makes `dist\uncharted-windows` and the zip.

Bloodborne by deadinside28, and on the [shadPS4

content.readme: # Lantern Engine Lantern Engine runs your own copy of Bloodborne on Windows and Linux: a launcher and my engine, built on bbport and shadPS4 and reworked by me for performance. The game's own code runs natively on your CPU; its graphics are translated to Vulkan. **No game files are included.** You need your own legal copy of Bloodborne (CUSA03173) with update 1.09, dumped from your own PS4. **Help:** [Help & FAQ](https://awakenchan.github.io/LanternEngine/): setup, a graphics settings guide, fixes for common problems and the beta guide. Bug reports go to the `#issues` forum on the [Discord](https://discord.gg/d3Uv3Cfr5x). ## Install 1. Download `LanternEngine--win64.zip` from [Releases](https://github.com/Awakenchan/LanternEngine/releases) and extract it anywhere. 2. Run `Lantern Engine.exe` and pick your game folder (the one with `eboot.bin`). 3. Press **Play**. The launcher updates itself. `Bloodborne.exe` starts the game directly (add it to Steam as a non-Steam game). ### Linux (beta) 1. Download `LanternEngine--linux-x64.tar.gz` from [Releases](https://github.com/Awakenchan/LanternEngine/releases) and unpack it (`tar xzf LanternEngine-*-linux-x64.tar.gz`). 2. Run `Lantern Engine` in the unpacked folder, pick your game folder and press **Play**. From a terminal: `./lantern.sh /path/to/CUSA03173`. 3. It needs a Vulkan driver (Mesa or NVIDIA), Python 3 and glibc 2.38 or newer (Ubuntu 24.04, Fedora 39, Arch, SteamOS 3.6, Bazzite). content.readme: # Playden for PS5 **Play your Steam library's Windows games on a jailbroken PS5.** [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/discord/1562443095629373590?label=Discord&logo=discord&logoColor=white)](https://discord.gg/wd8UjExpPA) [![Reddit](https://img.shields.io/badge/Reddit-r%2FPlayden__PS5-FF4500?logo=reddit&logoColor=white)](https://www.reddit.com/r/Playden_PS5/) Playden is a launcher that runs on the PS5, adapted from [Playden for macOS](https://github.com/leolobato/playden). You sign in to Steam with a QR code or your account name and password, browse your library, download games, and play them. The Windows games run through [prospero-win](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win), a port of Wine to the PS5. Each game gets its own private Windows environment and its own tile on the PS5 Home screen. > [!WARNING] > **Alpha software.** Playden is an early, experimental project. It signs in to **your real Steam account**, downloads > games with your licenses, and reads and writes your **Steam Cloud saves**. Read [Before you use it](#before-you-use-it). > If you are not comfortable with these risks, do not use it. ![Playden's library on the PS5: Steam games as cover art, with Installed, All, Favorites and Hidden on the side](docs/images/library.jpg) ## Features - **Steam sign-in with a QR code** (approve it in the Steam mobile app), **or with your account name and password.** Steam Guard email codes, Steam Mobile app codes and approval in the app are supported. The sign-in screen opens on the method you used last. - **Your whole Steam library.** Search, sort, favorites, collections, ratings and notes, with cover art and store details. The library works offline from a cache. - **Downloads from Steam.** Queue games and watch progress. The Queue screen also lists the games being prepared, in the order they start; Prepare next moves a waiting game to the front. - **Storage at a glance.** Settings › Storage shows how much space is used and lists installed games by size or last played. Select several games and uninstall them together; saves are kept unless you choose otherwise. - **Each game is its own PS5 app.** It gets a tile on the Home screen, so you can start it without Playden. - **A private Windows environment per game** ("bottle"), so games do not share settings or files. - **Steam Cloud saves.** Playden checks your Cloud saves before a game starts and syncs them after it ends. If the console and the Cloud disagree, you choose which one to keep. You can turn the automatic sync off in Settings and sync by hand from the Saves tab. - **Per-game settings.** Graphics, frame rate, resolution, controller mapping, and how the game starts: pick any program from the game folder, edit its arguments and library overrides, or try a game Playden flagged anyway. A game's settings can be exported as a recipe ([format](docs/community-recipes.md)). - **Graphics.** Direct3D 8–11 through [DXVK](https://github.com/doitsujin/dxvk), Direct3D 12 through [vkd3d-proton](https://github.com/HansKristian-Work/vkd3d-proton) (kit 0.11 and later), OpenGL through Mesa's Zink, and Vulkan, all on the PS5 GPU's Vulkan driver. - **Gamepad support.** XInput, DirectInput, Raw Input, Windows.Gaming.Input and the Windows multimedia joystick API, with rumble. Games see the DualSense as an Xbox controller, or, per game, as a PlayStation controller (a DualShock 4) for games that show PlayStation buttons; that choice needs a runtime kit with it. - **Local multiplayer.** Each signed-in PS5 user's DualSense is its own controller, up to four, for games with local co-op or split screen, through XInput and the HID gamepad APIs (runtime kit 0.18 or newer). Player 2 must sign in to the PS5 as another user (or a guest) with their own DualSense. - **Mouse and keyboard.** Plug a USB mouse and keyboard into the PS5, or use a controller preset: the left stick as a mouse, or the D-pad as the arrow keys. - **Import Windows games.** Add game folders you already have, from a USB drive, an M.2 SSD or over FTP. No Steam account is needed. See [Import Windows games](#import-windows-games). - **Install to internal or external disks.** Console storage, or an exFAT USB drive formatted on a Mac or PC. USB drives can change places: Playden and your games find them again. See the [compatibility list](COMPATIBILITY.md) for the games we have tested. ### Planned - Steam game updates - Other stores (GOG, Epic) - Support for game launches (Rockstar, EA, Ubisoft) - Community recipes in the preset chooser See the [roadmap](https://github.com/users/leolobato/projects/1) for what's coming next. ## Before you use it Playden is alpha software. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or supported by Valve. Know these points before you sign in: - **It is an unofficial Steam client.** Playden talks to Steam's servers directly, the way the Steam client does.

content.readme: # DriveClub Recomp **DriveClub for PS4 (version 1.28), running natively on Windows and Linux.** The source code is in this repository and the build is on the [Releases](../../releases) page. ## Join our Discord community: https://discord.gg/62b8jceumR ## Planned for the next major release - **DLSS/FSR Frame Generation, DLSS up to 4X, FSR up to 2X** - **Public online lobby** (being tested on our Discord first) - **Further performance and stability improvements** ## How to play 1. Download the latest `driveclub-recomp--win64.zip` from the [Releases](../../releases) page and extract it anywhere you can write to (not `Program Files`). 2. Have **your own** game dumps ready: - the **version 1.28 update** folder (it contains `eboot.bin`) - the **base game** folder (it contains `game000.dat`) 3. Double-click `DriveClub.exe`, press **Browse** next to each folder, check the settings and press **Play**. Nothing to install. Your own files are never modified or copied, and the folders you chose are remembered. Logs are in the `logs` folder. ### Linux (x86_64) The AppImage is built by the [AppImage workflow](.github/workflows/appimage.yml), or locally with `bash packaging/appimage/build-appimage.sh ` (see [BUILDING.md](BUILDING.md#linux-x86_64)). It uses the same game dumps and keeps its settings, prepared image, saves and logs in a `data/` folder beside the AppImage whenever that folder is writable (otherwise in `~/.local/share/driveclub-recomp`). Running the AppImage opens the native Linux launcher, with the same game folders, display, driving and patch settings as the Windows launcher. Press PLAY there and the recomp prepares and starts; `--play` starts it headlessly with the saved settings. Use DATA FOLDER > Change... in the launcher to select another folder or move the existing data. Put `update/` and `base/` next to the AppImage, use `--setup UPDATE BASE` once, or set `DRIVECLUB_UPDATE_DIR` and `DRIVECLUB_BASE_DIR`. The choice is stored in `data-path` beside the AppImage; `DRIVECLUB_DATA_DIR` overrides it, and a `portable` marker selects `data/` when no folder has been chosen. ## Highlights - The game's own x86-64 code runs directly on your CPU, with no CPU emulation. The PS4 system libraries are reimplemented and the GPU commands are translated to Vulkan, similar to Wine and DXVK - Playable from the menus through races, photo mode and saves, with trophies and multiplayer: private sessions with friends, and a public lobby that is being tested on our Discord - About 60 FPS at 4K in the heaviest scenes on our test PC (RTX 5070 Ti, Ryzen 7 5800X3D), higher in lighter ones, with an unlocked frame rate option in the launcher that keeps the game at its normal speed - Runs on NVIDIA, AMD and Intel graphics through Vulkan, with Resizable BAR used automatically where the driver allows it - Keyboard racing layout and any gamepad (Xbox, PlayStation, Switch Pro, 8BitDo) - Steering wheels with force feedback from the car's tyre physics, pedals with clutch, an H-pattern shifter and a USB handbrake - DLC content (add-on cars, bikes, tours and livery decals) can be unlocked from the launcher, built from your own game files. Cars you earn by playing still unlock through normal progression - A launcher window that resizes from every edge and corner and stays sharp at any display scale - A `mods` folder for loose-file mods: files in it replace the game's own files of the same path. See [Making mods](docs/MODDING.md) ## Controls Any gamepad works. Keyboard, mouse and gamepad can be used at the same time. ### Controller button prompts Button prompt icons can be configured in the launcher under **Driving > Controller buttons** (or via `button_prompts`, `xbox_buttons`, and `playstation_buttons` in `driveclub.ini`): - **Prompts**: `Auto` (automatically follows the controller in use, and shows key caps when you play with the keyboard), `PlayStation`, or `Xbox`. - **Xbox buttons**: `Xbox One` (modern flat A/B/X/Y buttons with View icon) or `Xbox 360` (glossy gem buttons with Back pill). - **PlayStation buttons**: `PS4` (the game's original symbols) or `PS5` (DualSense-style icons). | Action | Keyboard | |---|---| | Accelerate | W | | Brake / reverse | S | | Steer | A / D | | Handbrake | Space | | Shift down / up | Q / E | | Change camera | C | | Touchpad left / right half | R / T (R is Reset to Track) | | Accept | Enter / Z | | Back | Backspace | | Pause | Esc / P | | D-pad | Arrow keys | | Look around | I J K L or the mouse | F2 shows how far the clutch, brake and throttle are pressed, as bars with their percentage in the bottom left corner (a pedal at full travel is drawn bright and outlined; without a wheel it shows the gamepad's triggers). content.readme:
# Uncharted: The Nathan Drake Collection — PC port

Run the PS4 **Uncharted: The Nathan Drake Collection** (CUSA02344: *Drake's Fortune*, *Among
Thieves* and *Drake's Deception*) natively on Windows. The game's own x86-64 code runs directly
on the PC; a runtime supplies the PS4 system libraries, and a Vulkan renderer executes the PS4 GPU
work.

By **BilalReloaded** ([YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/@BilalReloaded/videos),
[GitHub](https://github.com/bc160201983)), October 2026. What changed and when:
[CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md).

> **No game files are in this repository or its builds.** You need your own copy of the game
> (the dumped CUSA02344 folder). This project is not affiliated with Sony, Naughty Dog or
> Bluepoint Games.

## Status

| Game | Plays | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Uncharted: Drake's Fortune | Yes | 60 FPS in the tested areas. Native rendering up to 2880x1620 (4K output upscaled from it, the HUD at 4K). |
| Uncharted 2: Among Thieves | Yes | Played at 1440p and 4K. 60 FPS and more; the heaviest view 99 FPS at 4K on an RTX 5080 (frame limit 120). |
| Uncharted 3: Drake's Deception | Yes | Played at 1080p and 1440p, 4K tested: the Cartagena crowd 90 FPS at 4K on an RTX 5080 (frame limit 120). |

The Collection menu, switching between the three games, saves, audio (music, speech, effects),
cutscene movies and controllers work. Details and open issues: [analysis/STATUS.md](analysis/STATUS.md);
plan and test list: [analysis/PLAN.md](analysis/PLAN.md).

## System requirements and the lowest PC that plays

- **Needs:** Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit); a CPU from **Intel's 4th-generation Core (Haswell, 2013)
  or newer, or any AMD Ryzen** (the games need AVX, F16C, BMI1, MOVBE and LZCNT); a graphics card
  or integrated GPU with **Vulkan 1.3** and a current driver; about **6 GB of free RAM** for the
  game (16 GB in the PC recommended).
- **Weakest GPU tested: the integrated AMD Radeon graphics of a Ryzen 7000/9000 desktop CPU**
  (2 compute units, about a quarter of a PS4's GPU). At **720p**: Uncharted 3 27-39 FPS,
  Uncharted 2 27 FPS, Drake's Fortune 24 FPS; at **540p** Uncharted 3 33 FPS. Playable, not
  smooth. Settings: preset **Low**, or resolution **1080p** with upscaling **FSR 1** at
  **Performance** (the game draws 960x540) or **Ultra Performance**, anti-aliasing off.
- **4 CPU cores:** 60 FPS in Drake's Fortune and Uncharted 3 (title screen and in play; a 4-core
  test with a fast GPU), with **Idle game threads: Sleep** (the default). On a 4-6 core CPU also
  try **Multithreaded rendering** (per game) and keep **Frames queued at 1**.
- **Players report:** Core i5-10400F + RTX 3050 6 GB plays Uncharted 2 and 3.

## Features

**Launcher** (`Uncharted Launcher.exe`)
- **Optional controller shell** (Settings -> System -> **Controller only mode**; off by default, the
  classic launcher stays as it was): a PlayStation 5-style home screen with a full-screen background
  and logo per game, and the three games on a carousel along the bottom. It opens on the game you
  played last, and moving between games dissolves one game's art into the next (the artwork is not
  shipped: see `launcher/assets/ps5/NOTICE.md` to add your own). The wordmark is
  top left; the **Games**, **Gallery** and **Display** capsules are across the top, with Settings and
  Quit as the gear and the power button top right.
- **Gallery:** your photo-mode pictures, in a grid with a filter per game and a full-screen viewer.
  It reads `Pictures\Uncharted Launcher` (or a folder you choose) and its `1 Drake's Fortune`,
  `2 Among Thieves` and `3 Drake's Deception` subfolders; anything you drop in appears on the next
  visit, newest first. Thumbnails are cached, so opening it again is instant.
- **Display:** resolution, upscaling and its quality, the frame rate limit, the display mode, VSync
  and the launcher animations in one panel, with **All settings** going to the full page. Left/Right
  changes a value; the settings pages and the config always agree.
- **Controller first:** the D-pad or left stick moves, Cross chooses, Circle goes back, Options
  opens the settings, L1 and R1 switch games (or filter the Gallery). Up from a screen reaches the
  capsules. **Hold L3 + R3** for two seconds to close a running game: the ring along the bottom
  fills while you hold, and the first five seconds after a launch are ignored so a controller
  resting on a desk cannot close anything. Settings -> System turns that shortcut and the on-screen
  hints off, and sets the hold time (1-3 s).
- **Controller only mode** (Settings -> System, off by default) picks the shell: on is the
  PlayStation 5 hub; off is the classic layout, with the game cards, the tab strip and the footer Play button, in the same
  window and with the same settings. It switches without restarting; both layouts work from the
  controller, and the keyboard still moves and chooses.
- **Settings** keeps every option below, as a category list on the left and the same rows on the
  right

content.readme: Kapitsa is an inference engine for Apple silicon that runs Qwen, Nemotron and Recursive's Flint models locally, built for coding agents. It starts opencode, Claude Code, Codex, Pi, Hermes, aider or Goose on a local model, and serves OpenAI and Anthropic APIs. [Quickstart](#quickstart) · [Benchmarks](#benchmarks) · [Features](#features) · [CLI](#cli) · [Models](#supported-models) · [How KFlash works](docs/kflash.md) · [Docs](docs/usage.md) · [Xcode 26 guide](docs/xcode-guide.md) · [日本語](README.ja.md) ## Quickstart **Requirements:** a Mac with Apple silicon (M1 or newer) and macOS 14 Sonoma or later. **Limits:** Apple silicon only: no Linux or Windows. # SkyboundTOTK

SkyboundTOTK is an experimental native static recompilation project for *The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom*, **base game version 1.0.0**. It targets Windows x64 and Linux x86_64. It is not affiliated with Nintendo. Expect graphical problems and incomplete compatibility; a successful build does not guarantee a complete playthrough.

The project's AArch64 game code is translated ahead of time into C and compiled locally into a native executable. A runtime implements the services the game expects, and the renderer translates its graphics work and shaders for WebGPU. This is a game-specific port, not a general-purpose Switch emulator. Some graphics translation still happens at runtime.

## Game files and distribution

You must supply your own legally obtained, already-extracted, **unmodified 1.0.0 base-game ExeFS and RomFS**. No game files, generated game code, keys, firmware or saves are included in this source project. The build does not extract NSP or XCI files. Version 1.2.1 also builds from its own ExeFS and the RomFS with the update applied (PR #19, contributed and tested by keno80: the build picks the hooks by the main module's build id); everything else in this README was tested on 1.0.0, and other updates are not supported by the game-specific hooks.

Keep your game files, generated code, executable package and saves private. The `game/`, `build/` and `dist/` directories are Git-ignored, but check what you are publishing rather than relying on ignore rules alone. The generated standalone package contains copyrighted game-derived data and must not be shared or committed.

## Build on Windows

### Requirements

- Windows 10/11 x64 and a GPU and driver supported by wgpu-native. Allow **at least 45 GB free in addition to the original game dump** for intermediate files and the separate packaged RomFS; the build is CPU- and memory-intensive. It runs as many compiles at once as fit in 80% of your RAM at 3.5 GB each (three on a 16 GB PC); set `RX_JOBS=<n>` to choose.
- Python 3.10 or newer on PATH, with `lz4` installed: `python -m pip install lz4`.
- Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools with the MSVC C++ tools and Windows SDK. Use an **x64 Native Tools Command Prompt** so the compiler can find the Windows headers and libraries.
- Clang, clang++ and lld. The build previously used emsdk 6.0.9: install it separately and set `EMSDK` to its directory (the lookup defaults to `C:\emsdk`), or put these LLVM tools on PATH. The build script does not download compilers or Python packages.

### Prepare and build

1. Put the extracted files in the project's `game` folder. The paths must look like this, not `game/exefs/exefs/main` or `game/romfs/romfs/Event`:

   ```text
   SkyboundTOTK/
     build.bat
     game/
       exefs/
         main
         main.npdm
         rtld
         sdk
         ...
       romfs/
         ActorSystem/
         Event/
         ...
   ```

2. Open an **x64 Native Tools Command Prompt**, change to the SkyboundTOTK directory and run `build.bat`. The launcher pauses at the end so you can read any errors.
3. The script checks the `main` and `sdk` module build IDs and a few RomFS directories, lifts the game code, compiles the native executable and copies the runtime and RomFS into `dist/SkyboundTOTK/`. The checks do **not** verify the entire RomFS or guarantee that a dump is complete.
4. Open `dist/SkyboundTOTK/SkyboundTOTK.exe` to run it. No command-line arguments are needed. Keep `image.bin`, `image.json`, `romfs/`, `wgpu_native.dll` and `SDL2.dll` alongside the executable. The standalone folder can be moved as a unit and does not need the original `game/` folder to launch.

The first lift and compile can take a long time. The builder reuses a completed lift only when its recorded game and lifter inputs match. If the lift was interrupted or those inputs change, move the existing `build/` directory aside before retrying. The script refuses to overwrite a nonempty `dist/SkyboundTOTK/`: move the existing package aside before a new build. Copy its `user/` folder into the new package if you want to retain its saves and settings. Do not delete your only save backup.

The package normally creates its own `user/` directory beside the executable; it does not automatically use the saves from another installation. Native renderer pipeline cache data is kept in `rxcache/` beside the executable. The executable also accepts an image path and `--romfs` / `--user` overrides for advanced use, but they are not needed for normal launching.

### Build and launch troubleshooting

- **Python or `lz4` missing:** install them for the Python on PATH, then reopen the tools prompt. Run `python -m pip install lz4` with that same Python.
- **Compiler, headers or libraries missing:** open the x64 Native Tools prompt and check that the C++ tools, Windows SDK, Clang, clang++ and lld are installed and discoverable. Set `EMSDK` if the LLVM tools are in a non-default emsdk directory.

# GTA: Vice City Stories — Native PC port (PS2 static recompilation)

A native **Windows and Linux** port of **Grand Theft Auto: Vice City Stories** (PS2, USA, SLUS-21590), made by
recompiling the game's PS2 executable into C++. Both are built from the same source and run natively: Direct3D 11 on
Windows, Vulkan on Linux.

**This repository contains no game code or game data.** You need your own copy of the game as an `.iso`.
The build reads the executable from your disc, and the finished game reads everything else from it while it runs.

Status: in development. See [docs/PROGRESS.md](docs/PROGRESS.md) for what works, and [docs/LINUX.md](docs/LINUX.md)
for the Linux build in detail.

## Install on Windows: the launcher (easiest)

1. Download the newest `VCS-Recomp-<version>-windows.zip` from the [Releases](../../releases) page and extract it
   somewhere short and local, like `C:\Games\VCS` (not Program Files, not a OneDrive-synced folder such as Desktop or
   Documents: the build writes thousands of files).
2. Start **`VCSLauncher.exe`** in that folder. It walks you through four steps, one at a time, then shows a big
   **Play** button:
   - **Folder**: the game is built in `build\` next to the launcher, or in a folder you choose (another drive with
     more room, say): *Choose another folder* on this step.
   - **Disc**: it looks for your `.iso` in Downloads, Desktop, Documents and its own folder; otherwise choose it (or
     drag it onto the window, or copy your disc from a DVD drive). It checks that it is the USA release.
   - **Build tools**: the game is compiled on your PC with Microsoft's free C++ tools. If they are missing,
     *Install build tools* runs Microsoft's installer with the right options (about 6 GB; Windows asks for permission).
   - **Build**: recompiles the game from your disc and compiles it, with a progress bar - 20 to 60 minutes the first
     time, a few minutes after an update. Nothing is downloaded during the build: the release brings Python and the
     libraries.
   - **Play**.

The launcher also backs up and restores your saves, makes a desktop shortcut, checks for a new release (only when you
ask, or at start if you turn that on in *Settings*), and zips the logs into a report for bug reports. Windows may warn
that the launcher is from an unknown publisher (it isn't signed): *More info > Run anyway*. How it works:
[docs/LAUNCHER.md](docs/LAUNCHER.md). Everything it does is a script in `tools/` you can also run yourself (below).
If the *Pricedown* font (GTA's lettering, free for personal desktop use from Typodermic) is installed on your PC, the
launcher uses it for its title and Play button; its licence doesn't allow including it, so it isn't.

## Install on Linux: the launcher (easiest)

1. Download the newest `VCS-Recomp-<version>-x86_64.AppImage` from the [Releases](../../releases) page. It runs on
   any 64-bit desktop with glibc 2.35 or newer: Ubuntu 22.04, Debian 12, Linux Mint 21, Fedora, Arch and later, on
   X11 or Wayland. It needs a Vulkan driver (Mesa or NVIDIA's) and `python3`, which every desktop has.
2. Make it executable and start it: in the file manager, *Properties > Permissions > Allow executing as a program*, or
   `chmod +x VCS-Recomp-*.AppImage && ./VCS-Recomp-*.AppImage`. The first start puts the game's files (the source,
   the scripts, the libraries) in `~/.local/share/VCSRecomp/install`, where the game is built, then walks you through
   the same steps as on Windows:
   - **Folder**: where the game is built (another drive with more room: *Choose another folder*).
   - **Disc**: your `.iso` from Downloads, Desktop or Documents, chosen, or dropped onto the window.
   - **Build tools**: the compiler (clang 19 or newer) and the libraries the build needs, from your distribution.
     *Install packages* asks for your password and installs them; *Install in a terminal* shows the command instead.
     On Ubuntu 22.04 and Debian 12, whose clang is older, it adds LLVM's own repository ([apt.llvm.org](https://apt.llvm.org)) first.
   - **Build**, then **Play**.

The AppImage is the whole launcher: *Add a shortcut to the desktop* in *Settings* puts it in your applications menu
too. Updates replace the AppImage itself (*Settings > Check now*); the next start puts the new files in place and only
what changed is rebuilt. Without FUSE (some containers and minimal systems), start it with
`--appimage-extract-and-run`.

# Pokopia Recomp

Pokémon Pokopia (Switch 2) recompiled to run natively on Windows.

[Download the latest build](https://github.com/drakolordx7/pokopia-recomp/releases/latest)

You need your own copy of the game, version 2.0.1a: an extracted folder, or NSP/XCI files plus your keys. Not affiliated with Nintendo, The Pokémon Company or Koei Tecmo.

- Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit
- GPU with Vulkan 1.3
- 16 GB of RAM

## Usage

1. Unzip the build and run `PokopiaLauncher.exe`.
2. Pick your dump folder (or your NSP/XCI files and key files) and press Set up. It compiles the game on your PC (about 7 minutes), then builds the shader cache (1 to 2 hours). You can pause it and continue later.
3. Press Play.

F1 opens the settings in game. Middle mouse toggles Joy-Con 2 mouse mode for placing items.

## Reporting problems

[Open an issue](../../issues/new/choose) with `pkp.log` from the session where it happened, your GPU and your Windows version.

- Code for this game goes in `recomp/games/pkp/` and `runtime/games/pkp/`; the rest is shared with other games.

Copy the game's `exefs` files to `game\dump\exefs\`, run `recomp\scripts\build_game.cmd pkp` in a Developer Command Prompt, then `pwsh -File game-build\scripts\build.ps1`. Shaders: [tools/shaders/README.md](tools/shaders/README.md). Launcher: `npm install`, `npm run tauri build` in `launcher\`.
- Runtime tests: `pwsh -File runtime\scripts\build.ps1 -Test`.

Built on [nxrecomp](https://github.com/drakolordx7/nxrecomp).
